title: Marketing Manager
description:
**Marketing Manager**
=====================

**About the role**
------------------

We are looking for a hands-on, strategic Marketing Manager to join the AltoVita team, reporting directly to the Director of Marketing. This is a broad role for a well-rounded marketer who is comfortable switching between strategy and execution: writing an award submission in the morning, running an event logistics call in the afternoon, and challenging the marketing plan when something isn't working. We want someone who brings ideas, questions assumptions and helps shape where AltoVita's marketing goes next, as well as delivering it.

**What you will achieve in your first 6 months**
------------------------------------------------

* **Win industry recognition.** Own AltoVita's awards programme end-to-end, with a focus on our priority awards (the EMMAs and Business Travel Awards). You will select the right categories, build the evidence and write winning submissions.
* **Deliver flawless events.** Take full ownership of event execution from A to Z, including our annual Smart, Safe & Sustainable Summit, industry conferences such as GBTA, ProcureCon and the AltoLive webinar series. This covers planning, budgets, suppliers, speakers, promotion, on-the-day delivery, follow-up and ROI reporting.
* **Raise our online presence.** Sharpen AltoVita's brand awareness and thought leadership, especially on LinkedIn, by shifting toward fewer, more strategic and higher-impact posts. Grow engagement and net new followers along the way.
* **Own the quarterly Corporate Accommodation Trends Report.** Lead the research, writing, production and promotion of each edition, and turn it into a recurring thought-leadership engine across webinars, PR, social and sales.

**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

* Develop and own the marketing content strategy, with content themes that resonate with our target audiences and align with company objectives and AltoVita's unique selling propositions.
* Shape and master the AltoVita voice on social platforms, building strong relationships with our audience, especially on LinkedIn.
* Craft compelling online and offline content, from SEO-driven and long-form pieces to thought leadership and product content.
* Identify the leading industry awards for AltoVita and write submissions ranging from 200 to 2,000 words. Manage deadlines, evidence gathering and stakeholder input.
* Research industry trends to produce whitepapers, benchmarking reports and industry reports, in collaboration with the demand and supply sectors AltoVita serves.
* Plan and run AltoLive webinars, including topics, speakers, moderation, promotion and repurposing content afterwards.
* Lead AltoVita's online and in-person event marketing, managing budgets and measuring each event's contribution to pipeline.
* Produce case studies and sales materials in collaboration with the Product, Sales and Customer Success teams.
* Contribute engaging content to email marketing, including the AltoVita newsletter and account-based marketing campaigns, in collaboration with the Director of Marketing.
* Contribute to PR initiatives by gathering data and stories for press releases and interviewing leadership and team members for news stories.
* Work closely with our in-house designer on all creative and graphic needs.
* Build cross-functional relationships to find storytelling and promotional opportunities, and support the Sales, Product, Supply and Customer Success teams with marketing initiatives that meet business objectives.
* Bring strategic input to the marketing plan. Challenge priorities, propose new channels and ideas, and use data to recommend where to invest.
* Measure marketing performance regularly across leads, pipeline influence, engagement and reach, and report insights and recommendations.
* Maintain brand standards and tone of voice across all communication channels.
* Keep learning about trends in corporate housing, serviced apartments, global mobility, business travel and hospitality.

**Requirements**
----------------

* 3+ years of B2B marketing experience across content, events and brand. Experience in hospitality, travel, global mobility or technology is strongly preferred.
* A proven track record of writing award submissions, ideally including wins.
* End-to-end ownership of events, both in person and virtual, including budgets, suppliers and ROI measurement.
* Exceptional written English with flawless grammar. Please be prepared to share writing samples.
* Experience producing research-led content such as reports, whitepapers or benchmarking studies.
* Experience growing a B2B brand on LinkedIn, with a strong grasp of thought-leadership content.
* Hands-on experience with HubSpot or a similar CRM and marketing automation platform.
* Strategic thinking combined with a willingness to roll up your sleeves, and the confidence to challenge and influence stakeholders, including senior leadership.
* Strong project management skills, consistency and attention to detail. You can juggle multiple deadlines without dropping the ball.
* A self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving, remote environment with high autonomy.
* Strong verbal communication and presentation skills, including comfort moderating webinars and representing AltoVita at events.

As the Senior Director of Design, Governance & Compliance at Vanta, you'll lead design for our largest product pillar. You'll set the direction for how compliance work moves from manual workflows to agents that do the work alongside our customers.

Governance & Compliance is the core of Vanta. It covers the frameworks, controls, policies, audits, and org structures that thousands of companies use to run their security programs. Those companies range from founders getting their first SOC2 to global enterprises managing hundreds of controls. As we move upmarket, the team's job is to make that complexity feel simple for every customer, at every size.

You’ll lead a team of senior, staff, and principal designers, with senior managers and directors reporting to you. You'll report to the Head of Design and partner as a peer with product and engineering leadership for the pillar. We're not starting from scratch. Vanta Agent works across the product, customers build and deploy their own custom agents, and our designers prototype and ship to production with our own AI design harness. Your job is to make that the way the whole pillar works.

* Lead the agentic direction for Governance & Compliance. Build on the agents we've already shipped, define what comes next, and shape how people and agents work together across the pillar
* Own design quality across the pillar. Set the bar, drive consistency from concept to ship, and get into the details yourself when it matters
* Design for platform and enterprise complexity. Lead the team through cross-cutting decisions on scoping, segmentation, org units, permissions, and multi-entity audits so the system holds together across surfaces
* Bring AI into how the team works. Build on our design harness, help every designer prototype and ship faster, and keep craft high as speed goes up

* Partner as a peer with product and engineering. Co-own outcomes and quality with your counterparts, not just the design work

* You have deep enterprise B2B SaaS experience. You understand custom configurations, multi-org workflows, and large deployments, and you've made complex products feel simple

title: Executive Director
description:
#### ***Thank you for your interest in joining Free Our Vote as our new Executive Director!***

**Location**: Remote

**Compensation**: $150,000 - $170,000

**Reports to**: Board of Directors

**Position**: Full-Time

**About Free Our Vote**
-----------------------

Free Our Vote uses data, technology, and rigorous research to expand access to voting rights, record relief, and economic opportunities for people with criminal records.We partner with nonprofit organizations, legal aid providers, government agencies, and researchers to identify people eligible for relief and make that relief easier to access. Our work combines court-data infrastructure, eligibility analysis, practical technology, and causal evaluation to help partners reach more people and understand what works.Originally focused on voting rights restoration, we have expanded into expungement and are developing applications in occupational licensing and other areas of economic opportunity. We are preparing a broader organizational brand and strategic plan that reflect this growing scope.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

We seek an Executive Director to lead Free Our Vote through its next stage of development. The Executive Director will work with the board and staff to sharpen organizational strategy, strengthen operations, expand financial support, and communicate the value of our work to a broader audience.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity in a small organization with substantial technical and research expertise and an established network of partners. The Executive Director will have responsibility for day-to-day management and execution of the board-approved strategy, supported by engaged founders and board members who contribute expertise, relationships, and strategic guidance.

The successful candidate will bring sound judgment, strong communication skills, and experience helping organizations navigate change. They will translate ambitious ideas into focused plans, support staff through implementation, and build the relationships and resources needed to sustain the work.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

### **Strategy and organizational change**

* Lead the development and implementation of organizational strategy in partnership with the board and staff.
* Guide the organization through its rebrand and evolving program scope, building a clear shared understanding of its mission and priorities
* Translate strategic decisions into realistic operating plans, budgets, responsibilities, and measures of progress.
* Assess new opportunities against mission, evidence, capacity, and financial sustainability.
* Lead organizational changes with clear communication, staff involvement, and accountability.

### **Staff leadership and operations**

* Manage and support staff, establish clear expectations, and create an environment of collaboration and strong execution.
* Own day-to-day decisions and ensure programs and partner commitments receive appropriate resources and oversight.
* Strengthen the processes needed for effective planning, financial management, and organizational administration.
* Work with the board and finance team to develop budgets and monitor financial performance.
* Keep the board informed about progress, emerging risks, and decisions requiring its involvement.

### **Fundraising and revenue development**

* Develop and execute a revenue strategy that combines philanthropic support with earned revenue from partner contracts.
* Cultivate relationships with foundations, individual donors, and other institutional supporters.
* Lead funding proposals, solicitations, stewardship, and renewals, drawing on staff and board expertise.
* Support the development and renewal of contracts that advance the organization's mission.
* Communicate a compelling case for investment in the organization's programs, research, and shared infrastructure.

### **Communications and public representation**

* Serve as an effective public representative with funders, partners, policymakers, the media, and other audiences.
* Lead communications and marketing strategy, including messaging for the organizational rebrand.
* Explain complex legal, technical, and research topics in accessible and compelling language.
* Represent the organization through strong writing, public speaking, and media engagement.
* Work with staff to share findings and practical lessons accurately and make them useful to partners and the broader field.

### **Partnerships and impact**

* Maintain and deepen relationships with nonprofit organizations, legal aid providers, government agencies, and researchers.
* Identify opportunities for collaboration that expand access to relief and economic opportunity.
* Work closely with technical and research staff to align organizational commitments with delivery capacity.
* Maintain a focus on measurable outcomes, rigorous evaluation, and learning from results.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Experience leading a nonprofit, social enterprise, program, or substantial organizational function, with responsibility for people, budgets, and results.
* Demonstrated ability to guide teams through organizational change, strategic shifts, or significant operational improvements.
* A record of securing financial support through fundraising, institutional partnerships, or related revenue development.
* Excellent writing and public-speaking skills, with the ability to represent an organization credibly to varied audiences.
* Experience developing or leading communications, marketing, or public-engagement efforts.
* Strong operational judgment and the ability to establish priorities and follow through in a small, evolving organization.
* Ability to work effectively with a board and engaged founders while exercising independent leadership.
* Commitment to expanding opportunities for people with criminal records and to using evidence to improve programs.

### **Preferred experience**

* Work in criminal justice, voting rights, economic mobility, access to justice, or related fields.
* Relationships with relevant philanthropic institutions, government agencies, or nonprofit partners.
* Experience with nonprofit technology, research organizations, or organizations combining philanthropic and earned revenue.
* Experience leading a rebrand or helping an organization communicate an expanded mission.

*Prior Executive Director experience is welcome but not required. We encourage applications from leaders who have demonstrated readiness to assume broader executive responsibility.*

title: Franchisee Onboarding Consultant
description:
Join the Goddard Systems, LLC (GSL) corporate team and help shape a nationally recognized leader in early childhood education!

GSL supports approximately 700+ Goddard School locations across the U.S., helping franchisees deliver high-quality, play-based learning to more than 100,000 children and families. Our corporate team drives the strategy, systems, and support that enable schools across the network to thrive.

**Position Overview**

The Franchisee Onboarding Consultant serves as the primary operational coach and consultant for franchisees entering The Goddard School system—through new franchise awards, new school development, or transfers of ownership. This role ensures smooth, compliant, and successful onboarding and transition experience while driving early enrollment growth and operational readiness.

From Building Permit or Letter of Intent (LOI) approval through 90 days post‑opening or post‑transfer, the Consultant partners closely with franchisees to guide school readiness milestones, surface and escalate risks, and build the capabilities required to operate a high‑performing, premium early childhood education school.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Franchisee Onboarding & Readiness**

* Lead a structured onboarding roadmap, ensuring timelines, milestones, and deliverables are executed as planned.
* Guide franchisees through operational and programming readiness standards, ensuring alignment with brand, licensing, and health and safety expectations (in collaboration with the health and safety team).
* Serve as the franchisee’s primary point of contact, proactively identifying and escalating risks to the Director, New Franchisee Training Program and internal partners.

**Licensing & Compliance Readiness**

* Monitor licensing progress and escalate risk when requirements, timelines, or approvals are at risk.
* Guide franchisees through licensing readiness milestones, including preparation for state licensing visits, health and safety inspections led by GSL, and required documentation.
* Provide ongoing guidance on childcare licensing requirements, background checks, ratio rules, health and safety standards, and state‑specific mandates.
* Maintain accurate documentation of compliance milestones for new schools and ownership transitions that occur via School Transfers.

**Enrollment Growth & Market Activation** Help franchisees develop and activate local marketing, community engagement, and enrollment plans aligned to opening and enrollment targets.

* Coach franchisees on lead generation, local marketing tactics, community partnerships, and high‑conversion tour experiences.
* Orient franchisees to FMS, Wonder of Learning including The Goddard Family Hub and outlining parent communication expectations.
* Monitor enrollment progress against targets, surfacing and escalating risk relative to opening dates and upcoming enrollment periods.
* Analyze enrollment and marketing data to identify gaps, adjust tactics, and implement corrective action plans when needed.
* Introduce tools that the franchise consultant will utilize such as the Annual Business Review, System Standards Review and Wonder of Learning Review (TBD)
* Ensure classrooms are tour ready, supporting the Wonder of Learning program, shelves contain learning materials and the school and classrooms are inviting.

**Staffing & Operational Capacity Planning**

* Provide guidance on staffing models to include recruitment marketing and hiring timelines to support enrollment growth and operational readiness. Franchisee conducts all hiring activities.
* Assess staffing plans in relation to licensing, ratios, enrollment pacing, and financial sustainability.
* Coach franchisees on leadership readiness, staff onboarding, and early operational routines.

**Transfer of Ownership & Changeover Support**

* Assess operational health and safety, licensing status, staffing stability, and enrollment continuity of the outgoing operation.
* Coach incoming franchisees through a structured transition plan, including coaching, training, GSL systems access, and licensing notifications.
* Provide time‑bound post‑changeover stabilization guidance focused on early indicators of enrollment continuity, leadership alignment, and operational stability.
* Ensure continuity of child, family, and staff experience throughout the ownership transition.

**Risk Management & Escalation**

* Surface readiness, enrollment, licensing, changeover, and stabilization risks early and clearly.
* Escalate risks promptly when expectations are not being met, partnering with cross‑functional teams to resolve issues.
* Monitor early warning indicators and intervene with targeted support to prevent downstream disruption.

**Coaching, Communication & Collaboration**

* Coach franchisees on curriculum implementation, school readiness, staff onboarding, and brand standards.
* Support franchisees through opening week and/or transfer week, and early operations to reinforce best practices and goal setting
* Provide bi-weekly progress updates to franchisees and internal stakeholders.
* Track milestones, risks, and performance metrics in internal systems.
* Build strong, professional relationships with franchisees and cross‑functional partners.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Business, Project Management, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
* 3+ years of experience in early childhood operations, franchise operations, school leadership, or multi‑unit field support.
* Strong knowledge of childcare licensing standards and regulatory compliance.
* Experience with onboarding, project management, or school launches.
* Exceptional communication, coaching, and relationship‑building skills.

**Preferred**

* Experience opening new childcare centers or supporting franchise launches.

* Staffing & Capacity Planning
* Risk Identification & Escalation
* Changeover & Stabilization Support

description:
**Healthcare Marketing | Full-time W-2 | Remote, U.S. (Nashville or Chattanooga based preferred)**
==================================================================================================

**About Clearstart**
====================

Clearstart is a holistic marketing partner built for healthcare companies navigating critical inflection points.

Marketing is at the core of what we do. We bring senior strategy and hands-on execution together in one connected team - helping healthcare companies build momentum, generate demand, and turn strategy into action.

Because growth rarely happens in a marketing silo, we can also bring in expertise across positioning, brand, web, GTM strategy, sales infrastructure, and the broader commercial organization, solving for the bigger picture without requiring clients to manage a collection of disconnected partners.

We plug in based on what a company needs. Serving as an embedded marketing team, providing senior leadership and strategy, adding execution capacity, or leading focused initiatives like a brand repositioning or website transformation.

We partner with select digital health companies, PE-backed care platforms, healthcare organizations, and payers navigating growth and change. Having sat in the CMO, CRO, and COO seats ourselves, we understand the challenges firsthand - from entering new markets and accelerating demand to repositioning for growth and preparing for what's next. We built Clearstart to be the team we always wished we had: senior operators working together, accountable to outcomes, and embedded enough to drive meaningful change.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

You know how to take a strategy, plan, or brief and turn it into polished marketing work that is ready to perform. At Clearstart, you will execute across a broad mix of channels, learn from senior healthcare marketers, and help clients move from good ideas to work that is actually in market.

**Work in Healthcare and Digital Health**

Clearstart helps B2B & B2B2C healthcare and digital health companies navigate critical growth and transformation points - from establishing market fit to scaling, expanding, and repositioning. You will support growth-stage and PE-backed clients working through long sales cycles, new markets, complex buyer journeys, and important growth milestones.

You will work in one industry, building deeper knowledge of healthcare audiences, buying cycles, and patterns across the portfolio instead of starting over with every new client.

**A Team Around You**

You will work within a multidisciplinary marketing team, alongside account leadership, strategy, coordination, creative, and senior healthcare expertise. You will receive strategic direction while still having the space to use your judgment, ask questions, and recommend a stronger way to execute.

You will not be expected to solve every challenge alone. You will be expected to own your work, communicate early when something is unclear or at risk, and collaborate with the right people to move it forward.

**Help Improve How the Work Gets Done**

Clearstart has an established delivery model, and there is room for you to make it better. As you learn what works across accounts, you will help strengthen templates, quality checks, channel best practices, and repeatable ways of working.

Your onboarding will include a structured ramp, a peer buddy, and regular feedback so you understand both the standard and the reasoning behind it.

**About the Role**
------------------

The Marketing Specialist is a hands-on marketing builder responsible for translating approved strategies, plans, briefs, and identified needs into high-quality execution across multiple channels. This role is for a well-rounded marketer who understands more than the tools. You should understand the audience, objective, and intended outcome behind the work; know how different tactics fit together; and be able to execute without needing every step spelled out. Depending on the initiative, you may receive a detailed brief or broader direction and guardrails, then develop the tactical approach and deliverables needed to bring it to life. You will own hands-on execution and QA, contribute tactical recommendations, and incorporate feedback through approved launch or publishing.

**What You'll Own**

* **Marketing execution.** Turn strategic direction and account priorities into polished, client-ready work.
* + Understand the objective, audience, message, and intended outcome before building.
  + Ask thoughtful questions and flag issues when direction conflicts with the strategy, timeline, audience, or scope.
  + Think beyond the immediate task by anticipating what else is needed to make the work successful.
* **Execution across channels.** Build and deliver marketing work across a varied client portfolio.
* + Content and thought leadership: draft, edit, repurpose, and publish content.
  + Organic social: create, schedule, and publish social content.
  + Email marketing: build, QA, and deploy campaigns, nurtures, and newsletters.
  + Integrated campaigns: build and execute coordinated components across channels.
  + Webinars, conferences, and events: support pre-event, live-event, and post-event execution.
  + Sales enablement and collateral: create and update presentations, one-pagers, templates, and related materials.
  + Customer and retention marketing: execute customer communications and supporting materials.
  + Website and creative assets: make approved content updates and coordinate web and creative production.
* **Quality of your work.** Own the accuracy, completeness, and readiness of everything you produce.
* + QA copy, links, formatting, functionality, targeting, setup, and other details before submitting work for review.
  + Ensure execution follows the approved direction and flag anything unclear, incomplete, or incorrect before it moves forward.
  + Apply feedback so the same issue does not have to be corrected repeatedly.
* **Delivery and collaboration.** Keep your work organized, visible, and moving across multiple clients and deadlines.
* + Manage assigned deliverables and communicate progress, dependencies, questions, and risks early.
  + Collaborate with account, strategy, coordination, creative, and specialist team members to move work from idea through launch.
  + Balance competing priorities without losing context, quality, or momentum.
* **Optimization and best practices.** Use performance and experience to make future execution stronger.
* + Monitor performance where relevant and apply learnings to future work.
  + Bring tactical recommendations, ideas, and channel best practices to account and strategy leads.
  + Stay current on healthcare marketing across B2B & B2B2C audiences.

**How You'll Know You're Succeeding**

* Your work consistently reflects the approved strategy, audience, objective, and brief.
* Account and strategy leads trust you to own the details, apply strong marketing execution best practices, and deliver high-quality work without needing ongoing coaching on the fundamentals of your craft.
* Deliverables are polished, accurate, fully QA'd, and ready for client review or launch.
* Work is completed on time, and questions, dependencies, or risks are communicated before they affect delivery.
* You can independently move work from direction to completion while knowing when to ask, challenge, or escalate.
* You apply feedback, performance insights, and best practices so your execution becomes stronger over time.

**Who You Are**
===============

You are someone who:

* Is a well-rounded marketer (marketing generalist) who understands how content, social, email, campaigns, events, sales enablement, customer marketing, and related tactics work together.
* Enjoys hands-on execution and can turn strategy, a plan, a brief, or an identified need into high-quality work.
* Uses sound marketing judgment rather than simply completing a task or operating a platform.
* Is proactive and solutions-oriented, anticipates what is needed, troubleshoots issues, and knows when to escalate.
* Has a high quality bar and notices the copy, link, formatting, targeting, and setup details that can make or break execution.
* Can move among multiple clients, priorities, deadlines, and types of work without losing context or momentum.
* Is curious, receptive to feedback, and motivated to keep improving the work and how it gets done.

**What You Bring**

* 3-5+ years of marketing experience.
* Healthcare, digital health, or health technology marketing experience; agency experience is preferred.
* Hands-on experience across multiple B2B and B2B2C marketing channels, including content, social, email, campaigns, webinars and events, sales enablement, and related tactics.
* Demonstrated experience independently executing marketing work from strategy, plan, brief, assignment, or identified need through completion.
* Strong marketing technology fluency, with experience working directly in platforms such as HubSpot, Salesforce, CMS and web tools, email and social platforms, analytics and reporting tools, and other client systems.
* Experience managing multiple deliverables, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously.
* Strong attention to detail and experience independently QAing marketing work.

**You'll Probably Recognize Yourself Here**

* You receive a marketing initiative/plan and immediately think beyond the requested tactic to the audience, channel, CTA, dependencies, and details needed to make it work.
* You enjoy building the work, but you also want to understand why it matters and how it supports the larger strategy.
* You catch the missing audience segment, unclear direction, or inconsistent message before the work reaches the client.
* When you do not know the answer, you clarify the need, determine the right next step, and find the information or person who can help.
* Bonus: you have worked with growth-stage, PE-backed, provider, payer, or digital health companies.

**Why Join Clearstart?**
========================

**What We Offer**
-----------------

**Base salary**

$70,000-$85,000 per year, based on experience

**Employment**

Full-time W-2

**Location**

Remote, U.S.; Nashville or Chattanooga based preferred

* A 30/60/90-day ramp with COO & Account Director, a peer buddy, training on how Clearstart works, and regular feedback.
* Clear decision rights and clear expectations for what strong performance looks like.
* **PTO**: Unlimited PTO and paid company holidays.
* **401(k) plan**: A 401(k) match of up to 3.5% after you have been with the company for one year.
* **TextCare**: Employer-sponsored virtual concierge medicine service, TextCare, access for you and your household.
* **Laptop**: A company-provided MacBook laptop.
* **Paid Leave**: Paid maternity and bereavement leave to support employees through important life events.
* **Profit-sharing program**: After one year of full-time employment, employees are eligible for annual profit-sharing contributions based on company seniority, KPI performance, and annual performance reviews.

**Our Core Values**

* **No Egos Allowed:** Work collaboratively without pretense, stepping up to support one another and deliver innovative solutions together.
* **Really Freaking Care:** Pursue every effort with a relentless commitment to excellence so that clients and colleagues thrive.
* **Adapt and Overcome:** Embrace change with agility to navigate challenges and unlock new opportunities for growth.

**Apply**

You will care about the client, the team, and the work at the same time.

title: Director, Logistics
description:
Finding the right place to grow your career isn't (over) easy, so we're here to help by sharing a few reasons why the grass is greener at Vital Farms. We think you'll appreciate our focus on Conscious Capitalism, which drives business decisions that benefit all our stakeholders (leading to even better business results). You might be drawn to our innovative approach and refusal to settle for the "way things have always been done." Or you could find it exciting to grow your skills while working for an industry-leading brand. Whether you're into our values, our brand, or our egg-cellent puns, we hope you'll join our Crew and help us change the world 108 square feet at a time!

At Vital Farms, we're proud of the diverse communities we serve and the stakeholders who help bring our purpose to life. We're committed to fostering an inclusive and collaborative environment where every crew member feels valued. We see this as one of our greatest strengths - and your role is key to helping us build on it.

**Your Role:**

This position reports to the Vice President, Supply Chain.

You know that great logistics is more than moving product from one place to another. It is how we protect quality, deliver for our customers, support our farmers and crew, and grow responsibly. You bring a strong mix of strategy and operational leadership, and you are just as comfortable setting the direction for the network as you are working through a transportation disruption, a provider performance issue, or a difficult cost and service trade-off.

At Vital Farms, you will lead our end-to-end logistics network across inbound farm transportation, outbound customer transportation, warehousing, cold storage, and distribution. You will build the systems, partner relationships, operating rhythms, and team capabilities needed to deliver reliable service, preserve cold-chain integrity, manage cost, and scale with the business.

**What You'll Do:**

You will own the logistics strategy and lead the team and external partners responsible for moving and storing finished goods safely, reliably, and efficiently across the Vital Farms network.

**Lead the logistics strategy and network**

* Set and execute a logistics strategy that supports Vital Farms' growth, customer commitments, stakeholder model, and evolving supply chain operating model.
* Own short- and long-range capacity planning across transportation, cold storage, warehousing, and distribution; identify constraints early and build practical contingency plans.
* Evaluate network design, lane strategy, storage footprint, and operating models to improve service, resilience, scalability, and total delivered cost.
* Translate logistics performance, risks, trade-offs, and required decisions into clear recommendations for Supply Chain and company leadership.

**Own inbound and outbound transportation performance**

* Oversee inbound transportation from farms and suppliers and outbound transportation to customers and distribution points.
* Lead governance for dedicated fleet and managed transportation partners, including routing, appointment scheduling, load building and optimization, tendering, carrier performance, freight claims, and special requests.
* Use on-time pickup, on-time delivery, customer scorecards, freight performance, and exception data to set expectations, drive accountability, and improve service.
* Serve as the senior escalation point for transportation disruptions, balancing immediate recovery with root-cause correction and prevention.

**Lead warehousing, distribution, and 3PL partnerships**

* Maintain overall accountability for receiving, storage, inventory handling, order fulfillment, and shipping of finished goods across the network.
* Manage and strengthen relationships with third-party transportation, distribution, and warehousing providers through clear governance, contracts, performance reviews, KPIs, and corrective action plans.
* Partner with site, Quality, and distribution leaders to maintain food safety, cold-chain integrity, inventory accuracy, pallet and load quality, and consistent shipment standards.
* Support new facility and distribution-capability readiness, including operating requirements, systems integration, launch planning, and transition into sustainable operations.

**Build financial and operational discipline**

* Develop and own logistics budgets and forecasts, including transportation, warehousing, distribution, accessorial, claims, and related operating costs.
* Identify cost drivers and loss areas, build fact-based recommendations, and deliver sustainable savings without compromising food safety, quality, crew safety, or customer service.
* Establish a practical KPI and operating-review cadence that creates one shared view of service, inventory flow, capacity, cost, risks, and actions.
* Partner with Finance and Supply Chain peers on forecasts, accruals, variance reviews, customer pickup economics, and business cases for logistics investments.

**Advance systems, data, and continuous improvement**

* Improve the integration and effective use of D365, transportation management systems, warehouse management systems, 3PL platforms, automation, and reporting tools.
* Connect operational data across internal and partner systems so teams can identify issues quickly and translate insights into action.
* Lead continuous improvement across transportation and distribution, including standard work, exception management, claims, inventory handoffs, customer feedback loops, and escalation paths.
* Partner with IT, Operations Development, and external providers to improve system reliability, visibility, controls, and readiness for future growth.

**Lead the team and cross-functional partnerships**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Logistics team with clear roles, priorities, decision rights, and accountability for results.
* Build strong working relationships across Farm Support, Operations, Supply Chain Planning, Customer Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, IT, and commercial teams.
* Create a culture of urgency, ownership, constructive challenge, learning, and recognition while modeling Vital Farms' values.
* Build team capability and succession depth across transportation operations, analytics, systems, partner management, and network leadership.

**What You Bring to the Table:**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Operations, Business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
* You have 10+ years of progressive experience in logistics, transportation, warehousing, or distribution, preferably in food, beverage, CPG, or another temperature-sensitive environment.
* You have led a complex, multi-node logistics network and managed third-party transportation and warehousing providers.
* You understand transportation markets, carrier and fleet operations, warehousing and distribution, cold-chain requirements, and relevant regulatory considerations.
* You can manage budgets, analyze cost and service trade-offs, and deliver measurable operational and financial improvements.
* You have experience with ERP and supply chain execution technology, such as D365 or a comparable ERP, TMS, WMS, warehouse automation, and reporting tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
* You use data and sound judgment to turn operational details and ambiguity into clear decisions and action plans.
* You communicate clearly, influence across functions, negotiate effectively, and lead through external partners as well as direct teams.
* You are a proven people leader who coaches, develops talent, and creates clear accountability.
* You are available to travel approximately 20-30% based on business needs, provider reviews, facility support, and network initiatives.
* Bonus points if you have launched or scaled logistics capabilities, facilities, automation, or major system integrations.
* You're no hero – You know the power of teamwork and celebrate the work of others before your own.
* You give a sh\*t – You believe in acting like an owner and making Vital Farms a place to be proud of.
* You raise the standards – You know growth can be hard, but you strive to improve yourself and others each day.
* You can walk in someone else's boots – You seek to understand other's viewpoints and think that you get to better answers by sitting on the same side of the table.
* You don't walk on eggshells – You're not afraid to leave the bullsh\*t behind and have honest conversations.
* We recognize that talent comes in many forms. Even if you don't meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. You may have strengths we haven't yet considered!

**What We Bring to the Table:**

* A fast-paced, energetic, remote environment with passionate people who are leading a movement to bring ethically produced food to the table.
* Competitive pay and benefits (Medical, Dental, Vision, and Paid Parental Leave, just to name a few).
* Generous retirement contributions: 401(k) + 3% Contribution from Day 1.
* Free eggs, along with friends and family discounts.
* Fun team SWAG that will make you the talk of the town.
* Professional development opportunities and an amazing team dedicated to your growth.

A reasonable estimate of the current starting annual base salary for this position is **$170,000 - $190,000**. Please keep in mind that hiring at the maximum end of the range would not be typical in order to allow for potential continued future salary growth.

**Who We Are:**

Vital Farms, a Certified B Corporation, offers a range of ethically produced foods nationwide. title: Director of Planning | Poppy & Peonies
description:
Bloom is a full-service workplace design consultancy, proudly supporting Poppy & Peonies in their search for a Director of Brand & Social to join their dynamic team. As Talent Advisors, we serve as the bridge between our Bloom Partner and you throughout the recruitment process. At Bloom, we don’t rely on automated tools to sift through applications—every resume is carefully reviewed by a real person to ensure a fair and consistent interview process. If selected, you’ll join Poppy & Peonies directly as a valued member of their team. We’re excited to consider your application! Please note that applications will be accepted throughout the holiday season. Thank you for your patience and interest in this opportunity!

  

Hi, I’m Natalie Dusome, Founder and CEO of Poppy & Peonies, a fun and energetic brand that believes styles and function should co-exist. We’re passionate about creating practical pieces that help make life a little easier and lighten the load, literally.

Building Poppy & Peonies has been a wild adventure. The journey began when my daughter Poppy was born and my accessories no longer worked with my new life as a mom, I needed bags with pockets and organization that looked cool and had functionality. I couldn’t find it, so I decided to create it, and in 2015 Poppy & Peonies was born.

We’ve come a long way in five years – from filling orders in my basement to appearing on Dragons’ Den, and now, expanding into new product categories and collaborating with some exciting influencers and brands. I’d be lying if I said it’s been nothing but smooth sailing, but thanks to our incredible community, we’ve never felt more loved and supported!

We believe in our responsibility to care for our environment and we are passionate about preserving the health and welfare of our planet, and the animals that live on it. All of our bags are made from high-quality vegan leather, and our entire product line is vegan, cruelty-free, and PETA-approved. We ship our products plastic-free and we use a combination of recycled, compostable, and biodegradable materials to mitigate shipping waste, and we are constantly looking for new ways to make our products and supply chain more sustainable to reduce our carbon footprint.

**About the Role**

The Director of Planning will lead the integrated Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Planning functions at Poppy & Peonies.

This role is responsible for translating commercial plans into actionable inventory and purchasing strategies, ensuring the right products are available in the right quantities, at the right locations, and at the right time.

Working closely with Merchandising, Product Development, Marketing, Finance, Sourcing, and Operations, the Director will establish a disciplined Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process that balances revenue growth, product availability, inventory productivity, and cash flow.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and financial acumen with hands-on planning experience in a fast-paced consumer products environment. They are comfortable working at both strategic and operational levels, building scalable processes while actively managing forecasts, inventory, and purchasing decisions.

### **The Opportunity**

**Demand Planning & Forecasting**

* Own the end-to-end demand forecasting process across all product categories, sales channels, and markets.
* Develop and maintain rolling demand forecasts at the SKU, category, channel, and distribution center levels.
* Partner with Merchandising, Marketing, and eCommerce to incorporate product launches, promotional activities, seasonality, marketing investments, and business growth assumptions into forecasts.
* Lead forecast reviews, analyze actual performance against projections, identify demand trends, and continuously improve forecast accuracy.
* Develop forecasting methodologies for new product introductions, core replenishment products, and seasonal collections.
* Identify demand risks and opportunities early and recommend actions to optimize sales and inventory performance.

**Supply Planning & Purchasing**

* Translate demand forecasts into actionable supply and purchasing plans, considering inventory on hand, open purchase orders, production lead times, transportation lead times, and safety stock requirements.
* Own the inventory purchasing plan and recommend purchase order quantities, timing, and replenishment strategies.
* Partner with Global Sourcing and suppliers to align production capacity, lead times, and delivery schedules with business requirements.
* Support new product launches by ensuring purchase orders and inventory availability align with launch milestones.
* Proactively identify supply constraints, potential shortages, and excess inventory risks, developing mitigation plans in collaboration with cross-functional teams.
* Balance product availability with inventory investment and working capital objectives.

**Inventory Planning & Optimization**

* Develop and execute inventory strategies across multiple distribution centers in Canada and the US.
* Establish and manage inventory targets, safety stock policies, and SKU classifications based on demand patterns, product lifecycle, and business priorities.
* Monitor weeks of supply (WOS), inventory turns, stock availability, and aging inventory.
* Recommend inventory allocation and replenishment strategies across markets and distribution centers.
* Identify slow-moving and excess inventory and work with Merchandising and Marketing on appropriate actions.
* Optimize inventory positioning to improve service levels while minimizing carrying costs, transfers, and markdown exposure.

**Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP)**

* Design, implement, and lead a structured monthly S&OP process, integrating commercial demand, supply capabilities, inventory investment, and financial objectives.
* Facilitate cross-functional planning discussions and drive alignment on a single, consensus-based operating plan.
* Partner with Finance to reconcile sales forecasts, inventory purchases, open-to-buy (OTB) plans, and financial targets.
* Provide leadership with clear visibility into demand and supply risks, inventory requirements, and key business trade-offs.
* Develop scenario planning capabilities to support business decisions related to growth, promotions, product launches, and supply disruptions.
* Establish clear planning cadences, accountability, and decision-making processes.

**Product Launch & Lifecycle Planning**

* Partner with Product Development, Merchandising, and Sourcing to support seasonal assortment planning and new product introductions.
* Develop initial demand forecasts and inventory buy recommendations for new collections based on historical performance, comparable products, and commercial assumptions.
* Align purchasing decisions with product development milestones, supplier lead times, and launch dates.
* Monitor launch performance and recommend inventory reallocation, replenishment, or exit strategies.
* Manage inventory planning throughout the product lifecycle, including introduction, growth, replenishment, and end-of-life.

**Planning Systems, Analytics & Process Improvement**

* Build scalable planning processes, reporting tools, and performance dashboards.
* Improve data quality, forecasting methodologies, and planning visibility across functions.
* Identify opportunities to automate manual planning activities and improve decision-making through systems and analytics.
* Develop standardized planning metrics, reporting cadences, and exception-management processes.
* Partner with Finance, Operations, and Technology to strengthen planning tools and data integration.

**Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Planning team, establishing clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and development plans.
* Build a collaborative, accountable, and data-driven planning culture.
* Serve as the primary planning partner to Merchandising, Marketing, Finance, Product Development, Global Sourcing, and Operations.
* Communicate complex planning information clearly and translate analysis into practical business recommendations.
* Drive cross-functional alignment and ensure timely decisions to support business priorities.

### **What You Bring to the Table**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Finance, Operations, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in demand planning, supply planning, inventory management, or integrated business planning.
* 5+ years of experience leading planning teams or functions.
* Demonstrated experience managing end-to-end planning in a consumer products, retail, fashion, accessories, or eCommerce environment.
* Strong understanding of demand forecasting, inventory optimization, replenishment planning, and open-to-buy management.
* Experience establishing or leading S&OP processes.
* Advanced analytical skills, including strong Excel and financial modeling capabilities.
* Experience working with ERP, inventory management, and demand planning systems.
* Strong communication, influencing, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with changing priorities.

**Preferred**

* Experience in a direct-to-consumer (DTC) business with frequent seasonal product launches.
* Experience managing inventory across multiple countries, distribution centers, and sales channels.
* Knowledge of international sourcing, manufacturing lead times, and ocean freight logistics.
* Experience with Shopify, WMS, and business intelligence or planning tools.

### **The recruitment process**

* Video screen with Talent Advisor from Bloom
* Video Interview with Yongyi, COO
* Video Interview with Nat Bates, VP of Finance
* Video Interview with Nat Dusome, CEO and Founder
* Reference checks
* Offer

Applications will be accepted through the end of November. Candidates can expect to hear from us regarding next steps by November 30th 2026.

### **Location**

* We’re seeking an exceptional candidate based in the US or Canada who values the flexibility of remote work while embracing the excitement of in-person experiences.
* There will be occasional domestic and/or international travel for photoshoots, events, and team retreats.

### **Salary and Total Rewards**

* Performance bonus

* Health benefits coverage
* $250 annual period & menstrual budget
* $1,000 annual allowance towards Poppy & Peonies product

However, we do not use AI to source, assess, screen, or interview candidates. title: Director of Talent Acquisition
description:
**Director of Talent Acquisition**

**About SSA**

Scientific Safety Alliance (SSA) exists to *Accelerate Science. Delightfully.* We provide mission-critical safety and compliance services to pharmaceutical, biotech, hospital and research organizations across the US, Puerto Rico, the UK and Europe. Since 2023 we have grown from $0 to $20M EBITDA with no outside equity (#175 on the Inc. 5000).

**The Opportunity: Director of Talent**

SSA has acquired 28 companies in three and a half years, and our ability to keep growing depends on finding, hiring, and keeping exceptional people. As our Director of Talent, you will oversee SSA's talent acquisition function and build our global talent attraction strategy across every branch in the United States, Puerto Rico, the United Kingdom, and Austria. You will lead our recruiting team and turn a decentralized, branch-by-branch approach to hiring into one scalable, global engine that brings in field service technicians, engineers, scientists, and corporate professionals at the speed our business demands.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who loves both strategy and execution. You will partner closely with branch leaders and the executive team to forecast hiring needs, build pipelines for hard-to-fill technical roles, build an employer brand that attracts top talent in every market where we operate, and give leaders the data they need to make good hiring decisions. You will also play a key part in our acquisition strategy, helping integrate newly acquired teams and planning the talent needed as each branch grows. If you want to build a best-in-class talent function at a fast-growing, employee-owned company, we want to talk to you.

**How You Will Make an Impact**

* **Global talent attraction strategy:** Design and execute SSA's global talent attraction strategy across the U.S., Puerto Rico, the U.K., and Austria, defining how and where we find talent in each market and aligning it with business growth, acquisitions, and branch-level forecasts.
* **Talent acquisition oversight:** Own SSA's full talent acquisition function, including recruiting operations, sourcing, hiring standards, and candidate experience, for every branch and corporate role.
* **Team leadership:** Lead, coach, and develop SSA's team of recruiters; set clear goals, manage priorities across branches, and build a high-performing, accountable culture.
* **Branch partnership:** Act as a strategic advisor to branch leaders and executives on workforce planning, role design, compensation positioning, and selection decisions.
* **Technical and field hiring:** Build sourcing channels and talent pipelines for hard-to-fill roles such as field service technicians, certification specialists, engineers, and laboratory professionals, including partnerships with technical schools, military transition programs, and industry networks.
* **Process and systems:** Standardize the end-to-end recruiting process, from requisition approval through offer; own SSA's applicant tracking system and recruiting technology, and hand new hires off seamlessly to the HR team for onboarding.
* **Global employer brand:** Build SSA's employer brand across all of our markets, including careers content, social presence, and candidate messaging, highlighting our employee ownership, culture, and mission to Accelerate Science. Delightfully.
* **Metrics and reporting:** Build talent dashboards covering time-to-fill, cost-per-hire, source effectiveness, offer acceptance, and new-hire retention, and use the data to improve results.
* **M&A integration:** Support due diligence and integration of acquired companies, including talent assessments, retention of key employees, and post-close hiring plans.
* **Vendors and budget:** Manage recruiting agencies, job boards, and talent acquisition budget to get the best return on every dollar spent.
* **Compliance:** Ensure hiring practices comply with employment laws in every country and state where we operate, including EEO, pay transparency, and background check requirements.

* A documented global talent attraction strategy, with clear sourcing plans for each country and role family.
* A single, documented recruiting process used consistently across all branches.

* Healthy pipelines in place for critical, hard-to-fill technical roles before openings occur.
* Strong offer acceptance rates and 90-day and first-year retention of new hires.

* Monthly talent reporting delivered to branch and executive leadership.
* A recruiting team that is well-trained, accountable, and consistently meeting its goals.
* Acquired companies integrated with key talent retained and hiring plans in place.

* Proven success building a talent attraction or employer branding strategy across multiple countries or regions.
* Proven success building or scaling a talent function in a high-growth, multi-location organization; experience in a private equity-backed or acquisitive company strongly preferred.
* Track record of hiring field service, skilled trades, technical, or scientific talent at volume.
* Experience with recruiting across multiple states and, ideally, internationally (U.K., EU, or Puerto Rico).
* Strong command of recruiting metrics, with the ability to turn data into action.
* Experience selecting, implementing, or managing an applicant tracking system and modern recruiting tools.
* Excellent influencing and communication skills, with credibility among executives, branch leaders, and candidates alike.
* A builder's mindset: comfortable creating structure where little exists and moving quickly.
* Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, or a related field preferred.

title: Child Sex Trafficking Navigator, Argentina
company: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children
description:
Independent Contractor Services
  
**Issuing Organization:** National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)
  
**Program:** U.S. Department of State–funded Child Protection Compact Partnership in Argentina
  
**Place of Performance:** Buenos Aires, Argentina, with travel throughout Argentina and periodic international travel
  
**Engagement Type:** Independent contractor (individual consultant). This is not an employment position.
  
**Period of Performance:** Base period from December 2027 through September 30, 2027, with up to four (4) one-year option periods. If all options are exercised, the engagement ends September 30, 2031.
  
**Announcement Date:** November 4, 2026
  
**NCMEC Contract Point of Contact:** John Shehan, Senior Vice President, jshehan@ncmec.org
  
  
1. Background
  
NCMEC is implementing the Child Protection Compact Partnership in Argentina, a five-year program funded by the U.S. Department of State that ends September 30, 2031. The program aims to strengthen prevention, victim protection, and the investigation, prosecution, and conviction of offenders, using trauma-informed, victim-centered practices.
  
NCMEC wants to engage one qualified Argentine professional as an independent contractor to serve as Child Sex Trafficking (CST) Navigator. The Contractor will focus on CST service mapping, professional training, multidisciplinary collaboration, and recovery planning. The Contractor will coordinate with NCMEC's Director, Argentina Child Protection & Strategic Engagement (the "NCMEC Program Director"), NCMEC subject-matter experts, the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Program Manager, and Argentine implementing partners.
  
  
2. Objective
  
The objective is to strengthen Argentina's national and provincial capacity to prevent child sex trafficking, identify and protect child victims, plan for the recovery of children missing from alternative care, and support the investigation and prosecution of offenders.
  
  
3. Scope of Work
  
The Contractor will perform the following tasks under work plans approved by the NCMEC Program Director. The Contractor decides how, when, and by what methods the work is done, consistent with the approved work plan, the deliverable schedule, and the contract terms.
  
  
**Task 1:** Prevention and Public Awareness
  

* Identify opportunities to strengthen Argentina's capacity to prevent CST, protect vulnerable children and survivors, and support prosecution of offenders.
* Work with local nongovernmental organizations to use NCMEC prevention resources to raise public awareness of the risk factors and vulnerabilities traffickers exploit, including online recruitment.
* Translate, localize, and promote NCMEC's "Guide for Parents & Guardians," "Guide for Child Welfare Professionals," and other relevant NCMEC CST resources, reflecting Argentine law, trends, and referral pathways.
* Liaise with provincial lead agencies and the Federal Council for Human Trafficking to improve victim identification, referrals, and sustained, child-focused prevention that addresses online recruitment.
* Strengthen coordination among civil society, technology platforms, educators, frontline personnel, and at-risk communities.

**Task 2:** Regional Resource Review and Response Mapping
  

* Review regional CST resources and response capabilities with authorities, civil-society organizations, and victim service providers.
* Map services, shelters, referral pathways, and agency responsibilities for children affected by or at risk of CST. This includes children missing from alternative care settings and children trafficked by parents or family members.
* Document service gaps, access barriers, coordination challenges, and regional differences.
* Use findings to inform CST and recovery-planning curricula for child-welfare professionals, law enforcement, and prosecutors.

**Task 3:** Professional Training and Technical Assistance
  

* Coordinate and oversee trauma-informed, victim-centered CST and recovery-planning training for judges, prosecutors, police, social workers, child-welfare staff, foster parents, mental health professionals, teachers, civil-society organizations, and family advocates, including multidisciplinary team members.
* Adapt training and resources, with NCMEC experts and implementing partners, to Argentina's language, culture, institutional structures, localized trends, and referral procedures.
* Deliver or co-facilitate training on CST indicators, online exploitation, running behavior, safeguarding, victim identification, recovery planning, and investigation and prosecution. Coordinate specialized instruction with NCMEC and Argentine experts.
* Help partners apply training to coordinated response, referrals, prevention of revictimization, and trauma-informed support for victims, families, and professionals.

**Task 4:** Recovery Planning for Children Missing from Alternative Care
  

* Provide technical assistance to strengthen Argentina's national CST recovery-planning framework for children missing from alternative care settings.
* Serve as NCMEC's liaison to child-welfare professionals and social workers whose caseloads include children who have run away, and connect them with resources and training on running behavior and response.
* Engage national, provincial, and regional leaders to review policies, plans, and practices for children missing from alternative care who are believed to be CST victims.
* Help partners clarify responsibilities, communication, referrals, and coordination before, during, and after a child's recovery, with emphasis on safety, continuity of care, and prevention of further exploitation.

**Task 5:** Multidisciplinary Teams and Specialized Investigative Units
  

* Share strategies, materials, and promising practices for effective CST multidisciplinary teams.
* Convene or take part in provincial and regional leadership meetings on team development, roles, referrals, appropriate information sharing, and coordinated victim support.
* Advise, with the NCMEC Program Director and NCMEC experts, national and regional law-enforcement agencies that are establishing or strengthening specialized child sexual exploitation and CST investigative units.
* Connect specialized units, child-welfare agencies, prosecutors, and victim service providers across Argentina's 23 provinces and the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires with one another, with national structures, and with NCMEC CST analytical and recovery-planning resources.

**Task 6:** Investigative and Prosecutorial Liaison
  

* Serve as NCMEC's liaison to Argentine law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors that do not currently receive CyberTipline reports but could use NCMEC analytical resources to identify CST victims and hold offenders accountable.
* Connect justice-sector partners with NCMEC resources, technical assistance, and expertise to support victim-centered investigations, prosecutions, and convictions.
* Liaise with PROTEX on support for CST investigations, prosecutions, and case integration across jurisdictions.
* Identify opportunities for collaboration between NCMEC experts and Argentine law enforcement on the role of gangs and organized criminal networks in domestic and international CST.
* Synthesize findings into recommendations on emerging trends, service gaps, coordination, and recovery planning, and escalate unresolved systemic barriers to the NCMEC Program Director.
* Maintain partner relationships, follow up on agreed actions, and contribute tools, documented practices, and knowledge transfer that will sustain the program's results.

**Task 7:** Work Planning, Monitoring, and Reporting
  

* Prepare and carry out annual CST work plans that define priorities, milestones, partner responsibilities, and implementation needs. Recommend adjustments as needed.
* Maintain timely records of regional reviews, trainings and participants, technical assistance requests and completions, meetings, recommendations, and follow-up actions.
* Collect supporting documentation and disaggregated data required by the program's Results Monitoring Plan, such as region, agency or sector, training topic, and audience.
* Provide verified activity data, attendance records, and supporting materials to the NCMEC Program Director and M&E Program Manager for quarterly reporting.

**Task 8:** Representation and Coordination
  

* Represent NCMEC at assigned meetings, trainings, working groups, and events, and deliver presentations on CST response, recovery planning, and project activities.
* Coordinate with relevant NCMEC divisions, including Analytical Services, Exploited Children, Family and Survivor Services, and Missing Children, to connect partners with appropriate expertise.
* Direct all media inquiries and public communications to NCMEC's Communications and Brand team. The Contractor will not speak publicly on NCMEC's behalf without prior written approval.

**4. Required:**  

* Argentine citizen/ legally authorized to work in Argentina.
* Must successfully complete NCMEC's background screening.
* Bachelor's degree in social work, psychology, criminal justice, human services, child protection, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
* At least five years of progressively responsible experience in child protection, child welfare, victim services, human trafficking response, or a related field, including substantive work with children affected by sexual exploitation or trafficking.
* Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary responses, service referrals, recovery planning, or related support for vulnerable children and families.
* Experience working with Argentine child-protection or child-welfare systems, government agencies, law enforcement, prosecutors, civil-society organizations, or victim service providers.
* Experience developing and delivering professional training, facilitating interagency meetings, and providing technical assistance.
* Experience in service mapping, regional resource assessment, or response-procedure review, and in turning identified gaps into practical recommendations.
* Demonstrated experience working and collaborating internationally.
* Full professional fluency in written and spoken Spanish and English.
* Able and willing to travel frequently throughout Argentina and periodically abroad.
* Registered with Argentina's tax authority (ARCA) and able to issue electronic invoices for professional services.

**5. Preferred:**  

* Advanced degree in a related field.
* Experience with children missing from alternative care settings.
* Experience with grant-funded programs, particularly U.S. government–funded programs, and performance reporting.

**6. Knowledge and Skills Expected:**  

* Strong knowledge of child sex trafficking, child sexual exploitation, associated vulnerabilities, and the needs of child victims and survivors.
* Practical understanding of trauma-informed, victim-centered, survivor-informed, and culturally responsive approaches.
* Knowledge of Argentina's national and provincial child-welfare, child-protection, victim service, law-enforcement, and prosecutorial structures.
* Ability to build credibility with agency leaders and frontline professionals and to facilitate collaboration across institutions.
* Strong training, facilitation, public-speaking, and written communication skills.
* Strong organizational, documentation, and time-management skills.
* Integrity, discretion, cultural competence, and sound judgment.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and with collaboration, training, reporting, and data-management tools.

**7. Contract Terms:**  

* Independent contractor status. The Contractor is an independent contractor, not an employee of NCMEC, and is not entitled to employee wages, benefits, or protections. The Contractor is solely responsible for all taxes, social security contributions, insurance, and registrations required under Argentine law.
* Schedule. The Contractor sets their own working hours. They must be available for scheduled coordination meetings, partner engagements, and time-sensitive matters, including meetings with U.S.-based NCMEC staff across time zones.
* Compensation. Will be discussed during the interview process.
* Travel. NCMEC must approve all travel in advance. Approved travel costs will be reimbursed at actual, reasonable cost under NCMEC's travel policy and applicable U.S. federal cost principles.
* Equipment. The Contractor provides their own standard office equipment. NCMEC will provide secure systems or devices for specific program functions.
* Option periods. NCMEC may exercise each annual option at its sole discretion, based on satisfactory performance, continued program need, and availability of U.S. Department of State funding.
* Funding contingency. This engagement is funded by a U.S. Department of State award and depends on the continued availability of those funds. NCMEC may modify or end the contract if the award is reduced, changed, or terminated.
* Termination. Either party may end the contract with 30 days' written notice. NCMEC may end it immediately for cause.
* Federal requirements. The contract will include the clauses required by NCMEC's federal award. These include anti–trafficking in persons requirements, debarment and suspension certification, conflict-of-interest disclosure, records retention, and access to records for audit.
* Confidentiality and safeguarding. The Contractor must protect the privacy, security, and confidentiality of children, survivors, families, and partners; apply child-safeguarding, trauma-informed, survivor-informed, and victim-centered practices throughout the work and sign NCMEC's confidentiality agreement.
* Sensitive content. The work may involve exposure to written, visual, or audio content about crimes against children, including child sexual abuse material, sex trafficking, other forms of child sexual exploitation and violence. The Contractor may access such material only through NCMEC-approved secure systems and procedures, and must maintain appropriate professional boundaries and wellness practices.
* Intellectual property. NCMEC owns all work products, translations, and materials produced under the contract, subject to the terms of the federal award.
